outcome: A May 2026 preprint by Colliot-Thélène and Schreieder proves ℓ-divisibility (up to torsion) results for the Bloch–Ogus coniveau filtration on motivic cohomology of smooth projective varieties over finite fields — a weaker assertion than, but directly bearing on, Parshin's conjecture — and gives an affirmative answer to their own open question (their Question 1.7, essentially a form of Parshin's conjecture for motivic cohomology) in special cases (i,n) where the étale cycle class map is known to be injective, e.g. i ≤ n+1 by Suslin–Voevodsky. This is progress/a partial special case, not a resolution of Parshin's conjecture itself, which remains open beyond dimension 1. No AI involvement was found anywhere in this history.
summary: Parshin's conjecture as stated in the frozen bullet (higher algebraic K-groups of smooth projective varieties over finite fields vanish up to torsion) remains open in general, proven only for dim 0 (Quillen) and dim 1 (Harder), as the problem's own Wikipedia article confirms with no update since 2024. Two items surfaced in triage and in my own search. (1) arXiv:2011.05544 'Proof of the Parshin's Conjecture' by Aydin Yousefzadehfard: verified via the arXiv abstract/comment page that this was withdrawn by the author on 2020-11-21 (v2), with the author's own comment identifying a flaw in Theorem 4.7 ('There is a problem with the Theorem 4.7... it ruins the double deformation construction'). It never entered the literature as a proof, and in any case its only activity (submission and withdrawal) is from November 2020, well before the 26 January 2024 frozen-revision date — it is not an event in the window at all, not even open_stale material, since nothing about it changed after 2024. (2) arXiv:2605.22494 'Divisibility phenomena in motivic Bloch–Ogus theory' by Colliot-Thélène and Schreieder, submitted 21 May 2026 (within the window): I fetched the full HTML text and located the paper's explicit discussion of Parshin's conjecture in §1.3, where the authors state Parshin's conjecture predicts H_M^i(X,Z(n))⊗Q_ℓ = 0 for i ≠ 2n, and then say their Theorem 1.4 proves 'the weaker assertion' that the Bloch–Ogus filtration step L_j vanishes after tensoring with Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ for j<n. They pose their own open Question 1.7 asking whether the full statement (a form of Parshin's conjecture for motivic cohomology with Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ coefficients) holds, and in Appendix C give an affirmative answer to that question in special cases (i,n) where the relevant étale cycle class map is injective — which by Suslin–Voevodsky covers i ≤ n+1. This is a genuine, dated, primary-sourced piece of progress: a bound/partial-vanishing result that is explicitly framed by the authors themselves as bearing on Parshin's conjecture, restricted to special cases, not a full resolution — hence `progress` rather than `partial` or `resolved`, since the general conjecture (all i, all n, all smooth projective X/finite field, all dimensions) is untouched and the authors' own Question 1.7 (closer to the actual conjecture) is left open outside those special cases. I separately verified an earlier item mentioned by triage's search context, a 2023 paper ('Motivic cohomology and K-theory of some surfaces over finite fields', published in J. Pure Appl. Algebra / J. London Math. Soc., August 2023) whose appendix 'slightly enlarges the class of surfaces for which Parshin's conjecture is known' — but this predates the frozen revision date (published 2023, and referenced already-existing arXiv work), so even if its arXiv posting is confirmed pre-2024 it is not a window event; I was unable to find its exact arXiv ID/submission date via search, so I have not counted it as an event either way, noting the gap in `incomplete`. I found no mention of AI, LLMs, Lean/Coq formalization, or any computational proof assistant anywhere in the 2026 Colliot-Thélène–Schreieder paper (checked its full text and acknowledgements) or in any secondary source discussing Parshin's conjecture; this is standard human-authored pure mathematics.
competing_reading: One could argue this is not really progress on 'Parshin's conjecture' as Wikipedia's bullet states it (K-groups vanish up to torsion) but rather progress on a related-but-distinct motivic-cohomology reformulation (vanishing of H_M^i(X,Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(n)) for i≠2n), which the paper's own Question 1.7 treats as a question in its own right rather than as identical to Parshin's original K-theoretic statement — under the strict §3.1 scope rule this could be read as a 'related problem' (a reformulation with different objects, motivic cohomology groups rather than K-groups) rather than a 'case' of the stated problem, which would make the correct status `open` with `no_change_found` true rather than `progress`. I lean toward `progress` because the authors themselves present their motivic-cohomology statement as the natural refinement/reformulation of Parshin's conjecture (citing the standard motivic spectral sequence relating K-theory and motivic cohomology, under which the K-theoretic vanishing follows from the motivic one), and because they explicitly answer their own question — which is essentially Parshin's conjecture stated in motivic-cohomological terms — affirmatively in nontrivial special cases.
what_would_settle_it: A citation or explicit statement in the paper (or a companion source) spelling out the precise implication from their motivic-cohomology vanishing statement to K_i(X)⊗Q = 0 (i.e. via the motivic spectral sequence converging to K-theory), which would confirm the special cases in Appendix C are literally cases of the K-theoretic Parshin conjecture and not merely a cohomological analogue; and locating the exact arXiv submission date of the 2023 Gregory/appendix surfaces paper to confirm it is indeed pre-window.
